legend: After learning about polynomial hashing, Heidi decided to learn about shift-xor hashing. In particular, she came across this interesting problem.
Given a bitstring y∈{0,1}n%%ZSMJ0%% find out the number of different k%%ZSMJ1%% (0≤k<n%%ZSMJ2%%) such that there exists x∈{0,1}n%%ZSMJ3%% for which y=x⊕shiftk(x).%%ZSMJ4%%

In the above, ⊕%%ZSMJ5%% is the xor operation and shiftk%%ZSMJ6%% is the operation of shifting a bitstring cyclically to the right k%%ZSMJ7%% times. For example, 001⊕111=110%%ZSMJ8%% and shift3(00010010111000)=00000010010111%%ZSMJ9%%.
input: The first line contains an integer n%%ZSMJ10%% (1≤n≤2⋅105%%ZSMJ11%%), the length of the bitstring y%%ZSMJ12%%.
The second line contains the bitstring y%%ZSMJ13%%.
output: Output a single integer: the number of suitable values of k%%ZSMJ14%%.
note: There is no x%%ZSMJ18%% such that x⊕x=1010%%ZSMJ19%%, hence the answer is 3%%ZSMJ20%%.
